title: Machine-Checked Exact-Rational Adjugate Perron, Treeplex Stability, and UTC Separation Certificates for Sub-Sqrt(T) Linear Swap Regret in Polyhedral Games
abstract: Vasilis Pollatos and Alberto Marchesi (arXiv:2611.33081, November 24, 2026) broke the sqrt(T) cumulative regret barrier for linear swap regret in self-play over polyhedral games: their deterministic uncoupled optimistic log-barrier dynamics achieve O~(poly(D) T^{1/3}) cumulative linear Phi-regret on arbitrary compact H-polytopes (independent of vertex count) and O(n^2 M^4 log(T+1)) in n-player perfect-recall extensive-form games (EFGs) with at most M terminal sequences per player, extending logarithmic trigger-regret rates to all untimed-communication (UTC) linear deviations. We present a machine-checked, zero-floating-point formalization and exact-Q certificate auditor for the algebraic, adjugate-Perron, stability-to-regret, and UTC-vs-trigger separation core of this breakthrough. First, an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (LinearSwapRegretPolyhedral.lean, Lean 4.35.0; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice) formalizes the Lemma 3 path-length bridge (a+b)^2 <= 2(a^2+b^2), Theorem 4 self-play energy cancellation gamma^2 >= 128 n^2 C_*, Eq. (13) parameter choice gamma = 320 n M^2 with 4x exact square margin, T^{1/3} exponent balance at lambda = T^{-2/3}, Appendix G's exact sensitivity chain (2r^2 + r/2 <= (5/2)r^2, (5/2)^2 * 32 = 200, exact Mercator certification log 2 < 23581/34020 < 11/15 => g(2) > 4/15 > 1/16), exact 2x2 column-stochastic adjugate Perron fixed-point and monotonicity identities, Euler derivative bounds |rho'(0)| <= r rho(0), multi-player Cauchy-Schwarz, reset fixed-point contraction, and an exhaustive 16-trigger proof of the Student-Professor UTC gain 3T/2. Second, SWAP-POLYHEDRAL-CERT-1.0 audits four exact-Q modes across 16 canonical certificates (0.192-6.384 ms) and rejects 62/62 live adversarial forgeries.
